data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR):
Is the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for assessing the suitability of personnel to access USDA information resources;
Sets the criteria for personnel to gain and maintain access to USDA information and information systems; and
Defines the standards by which personnel establish and maintain a level of trust (e.g., suitability, fitness, and credentialing).
policy_statements.target: standards by which personnel establish and maintain a level of trust

policy_statements.source_text: This DR serves as the foundation for Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices to develop and implement their own personnel security procedures.
policy_statements.target: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: This DR meets the requirements of:
The Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), 44 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 3551, et seq.;
cross_references: The Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), 44 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 3551, et seq.

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Circular A-123, Management’s Responsibility for Enterprise Risk Management and Internal Control, Memorandum M-16-17;
cross_references: The Office of Management and Budget (OMB), Circular A-123, Management’s Responsibility for Enterprise Risk Management and Internal Control, Memorandum M-16-17

policy_statements.source_text: OMB Circular A-130, Managing Information as a Strategic Resource;
cross_references: OMB Circular A-130, Managing Information as a Strategic Resource

policy_statements.source_text: The National Institutes of Standards and Technology (NIST) Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems; and
cross_references: The National Institutes of Standards and Technology (NIST) Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems

policy_statements.source_text: The personnel security family of controls in NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Revision 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations.
cross_references: NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Revision 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA:
Complies with Federal requirements to assess suitability and fitness of USDA personnel to access USDA information and information systems;
policy_statements.target: suitability and fitness of USDA personnel

policy_statements.source_text: Confirms its management commitment to comply with the authorities governing USDA personnel security for access to information and information systems;
policy_statements.target: authorities governing USDA personnel security for access to information and information systems

policy_statements.source_text: Supports personnel security activities for protecting USDA information and information systems; and
Continually manages risks to those systems.
This DR is effective when published and will remain in effect until superseded or expired.
conditions: when published
until superseded or expired

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will align their procedures with this policy within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: This DR is a supplement to DR 4720-001, USDA Onboarding Requirements.
cross_references: DR 4720-001, USDA Onboarding Requirements

policy_statements.source_text: This policy applies to:
All Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, and all USDA personnel;
policy_statements.target: All Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, and all USDA personnel

policy_statements.source_text: Information, information systems, and cloud-based services used or operated by, for, or on behalf of USDA.
policy_statements.target: Information, information systems, and cloud-based services used or operated by, for, or on behalf of USDA

policy_statements.source_text: These include interconnections between or among these information systems or services; and
policy_statements.target: interconnections between or among these information systems or services

Facilities owned or operated by USDA; or
policy_statements.target: Facilities owned or operated by USDA

policy_statements.source_text: This policy guides senior executives and managers to provide the resources necessary to establish:
Eligibility for employment;
The identity, suitability, and fitness of personnel to perform work for, or on behalf of, the USDA; and
policy_statements.target: identity, suitability, and fitness of personnel to perform work for, or on behalf of, the USDA

policy_statements.source_text: Procedures to issue USDA credentials for access to Federal buildings and USDA information systems.
policy_statements.target: Procedures to issue USDA credentials for access to Federal buildings and USDA information systems

policy_statements.source_text: Nothing in this policy alters the requirements for protecting national security systems or information.
policy_statements.target: requirements for protecting national security systems or information

policy_statements.source_text: This includes those identified in FISMA and the Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS) policies and standards.
cross_references: FISMA
Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS) policies and standards

policy_statements.source_text: It also includes intelligence community policies, directives, and instructions.
USDA personnel hold roles with a variety of privileges and access.
Personnel are vital in protecting USDA information and information systems.
Personnel must act responsibly with their privileges and access.
As such, USDA personnel must also guard against malicious use or exploitation of legitimate access, per DR 4600-003, USDA Defensive Counterintelligence and Insider Threat Programs.
cross_references: DR 4600-003, USDA Defensive Counterintelligence and Insider Threat Programs
policy_statements.target: malicious use or exploitation of legitimate access

policy_statements.source_text: The unauthorized disclosure, access, use, disruption, modification, destruction, or the loss of control of sensitive information can erode public trust in USDA.
It can also cause adverse financial impacts to USDA.
Security techniques establish suitable levels of trust for USDA personnel.
These techniques include background investigations, assigning a risk designation to each position, completing access agreements, managing privileges, and terminating access in a timely manner.
All of these can also minimize risks to USDA information and information systems.
Each Mission Area, agency, and staff office will:
Develop and implement procedures that address personnel suitability standards described in this DR for granting access to USDA information and information systems;
policy_statements.actor_name: Each Mission Area, agency, and staff office
policy_statements.target: procedures that address personnel suitability standards described in this DR for granting access to USDA information and information systems
conditions: that address personnel suitability standards described in this DR for granting access to USDA information and information systems

policy_statements.actor_name: Each Mission Area, agency, and staff office

policy_statements.actor_name: Each Mission Area, agency, and staff office

policy_statements.source_text: Assign position risk designations and sensitivity levels for all Government and contractor positions;
policy_statements.actor_name: Each Mission Area, agency, and staff office

policy_statements.source_text: Review the position designations at least annually; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Each Mission Area, agency, and staff office

policy_statements.actor_name: Each Mission Area, agency, and staff office
cross_references: Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Position Designation Automated Tool (PDT)
conditions: as needed

policy_statements.source_text: The procedures will:
Require USDA personnel to obtain and maintain favorable background investigations, based on the position sensitivity levels and risk designations;
conditions: based on the position sensitivity levels and risk designations

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that USDA personnel receive favorable background investigations or Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) fingerprint checks (per DM 4620-002) that meet or exceed the requirements for the intended positions;
conditions: that meet or exceed the requirements for the intended positions

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure USDA personnel submit their background investigation requests to Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA);
Note: See the DCSA website Requesting Personnel Investigations via e-QIP, for additional information.
cross_references: DCSA website Requesting Personnel Investigations via e-QIP

policy_statements.source_text: Allow for the reciprocal use of current and favorable background investigations from other Federal agencies, as long as they meet or exceed the requirements for the intended positions.
policy_statements.target: reciprocal use of current and favorable background investigations from other Federal agencies
conditions: as long as they meet or exceed the requirements for the intended positions

policy_statements.source_text: Allow managers or Contracting Officer’s Representatives (COR) to request approval for personnel to begin performing some duties, per DM 4620-002:
After they submit their background investigation forms to the DCSA; and
conditions: After they submit their background investigation forms to the DCSA

policy_statements.source_text: The FBI fingerprint check does not return derogatory information.
conditions: The FBI fingerprint check does not return derogatory information

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure managers follow the guidance in DR 3440-001, USDA Classified National Security Information Program Regulation and DR 4600-001 if the position requires access to classified information.
cross_references: DR 3440-001, USDA Classified National Security Information Program Regulation
conditions: if the position requires access to classified information

policy_statements.source_text: The procedures for granting access to USDA information or systems will include processes to:

Update background investigations when USDA personnel change positions (e.g., relocation or promotion) or the position requirements change (e.g., additional access to more sensitive or classified materials), per DR 3440-001, DR 4600-001, and DR 3440-003, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Program; and
cross_references: DR 3440-003, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Program
conditions: when USDA personnel change positions (e.g., relocation or promotion) or the position requirements change (e.g., additional access to more sensitive or classified materials)

policy_statements.source_text: Add, remove, or change physical or logical access, as needed, when USDA personnel change duties or locations within USDA.
conditions: as needed
when USDA personnel change duties or locations within USDA

policy_statements.source_text: The procedures will require all personnel to sign access agreements that:
Define their personal responsibilities;
Inform them of appropriate use, conduct, actions, and behavior permitted on, or when using, Departmental information systems; and
Serve to acknowledge that they understand these conditions.
Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will:
Develop and document access agreements based on information type and sensitivity level for each category of information or information system;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: based on information type and sensitivity level

policy_statements.source_text: Review the agreements at least annually and update them as needed;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: at least annually
as needed

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that USDA personnel:
Acknowledge their understanding of the access agreement, by handwritten or digital signature, prior to being granted access to information and information systems; and
policy_statements.target: their understanding of the access agreement
conditions: prior to being granted access to information and information systems

policy_statements.source_text: Review and acknowledge the access agreement annually, or when the agreement is updated.
conditions: annually, or when the agreement is updated

policy_statements.source_text: Describe acceptable and improper uses of information systems that include:
A provision that USDA personnel are permitted access to, and use of, USDA systems to carry out their USDA responsibilities; and
A clear explanation that limited personal use of USDA information systems is allowed but does not extend to improper use of the systems.
Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will develop procedures and implement measures to prevent, detect, track, and report improper use.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: The following activities are prohibited and amount to improper use of USDA information systems:
Intentionally changing or attempting to change information security controls that protect against unauthorized access;
policy_statements.target: information security controls that protect against unauthorized access

policy_statements.source_text: Downloading unauthorized software, such as peer-to-peer sharing apps and illegal or copyrighted materials;
policy_statements.target: unauthorized software, such as peer-to-peer sharing apps and illegal or copyrighted materials

policy_statements.source_text: Distributing illegally-obtained files or software;
Permitting or enabling unauthorized access to any USDA information system for any purpose;
Engaging in inappropriate activities or those likely to offend fellow employees or the public.
This includes:
Accessing sexually explicit materials; and
Using hate speech or remarks to ridicule others based on age, race, creed, religion, skin color, sex, physical or mental handicap, or national origin.
Accessing or attempting to access any USDA information system for unauthorized purposes, such as:
Invasion of privacy; and
Obtaining information that the user is not authorized to access, use, disclose, modify, or destroy.
policy_statements.target: information that the user is not authorized to access, use, disclose, modify, or destroy

policy_statements.source_text: The procedures for personnel departing USDA (permanently or temporarily) will include the follow:
Retrieve all USDA-issued property, assets, and systems;
policy_statements.target: all USDA-issued property, assets, and systems

policy_statements.source_text: Transfer any sensitive information to an authorized individual;
Disable all physical and logical access;
Archive and disable information system accounts, per DR 3505-003; and
Follow guidance in DR 4600-002, Procedures for the Denial or Revocation of Access to National Security Information, when involving access to classified information or systems.
cross_references: DR 4600-002, Procedures for the Denial or Revocation of Access to National Security Information
conditions: when involving access to classified information or systems

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will ensure that contracts and other agreements with external providers include requirements to:

Ensure that personnel security processes, such as on-boarding, off-boarding, and reassignments, meet or exceed USDA personnel security requirements in this policy and in DR 4020-250-002, Position Management and Vacancy Control;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
cross_references: DR 4020-250-002, Position Management and Vacancy Control

policy_statements.source_text: Notify USDA Contracting Officers and CORs of personnel changes to contracted services (e.g., adding or removing personnel to contract support staff).
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: This enables timely granting, modifying, or suspension of access rights and privileges, and the return of Government-furnished equipment; and
Provide their documented personnel security processes, as evidence of compliance.

Lead the Departmental information security program;
Develop and implement the USDA information security program plan;
Ensure the program plan includes suitability standards defined in this DR and the Personnel Security control family in NIST SP 800-53, Revision 5;

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure compliance with the information security program across the USDA.

extract_result.scope:
a. This policy applies to:
(1) All Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, and all USDA personnel;
(2) Information, information systems, and cloud-based services used or operated by, for, or on behalf of USDA. These include interconnections between or among these information systems or services; and
(3) Facilities from which these information systems or services operate, including:
(a) Facilities owned or operated by USDA; or
(b) Facilities owned or operated on behalf of USDA by a contractor, subcontractor, or other organization.
b. This policy guides senior executives and managers to provide the resources necessary to establish:
(1) Eligibility for employment;
(2) The identity, suitability, and fitness of personnel to perform work for, or on behalf of, the USDA; and
(3) Procedures to issue USDA credentials for access to Federal buildings and USDA information systems.
c. Nothing in this policy alters the requirements for protecting national security systems or information. This includes those identified in FISMA and the Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS) policies and standards. It also includes intelligence community policies, directives, and instructions.

The unauthorized disclosure, access, use, disruption, modification, destruction, or the loss of control of sensitive information can erode public trust in USDA.
It can also cause adverse financial impacts to USDA.
Security techniques establish suitable levels of trust for USDA personnel.
These techniques include background investigations, assigning a risk designation to each position, completing access agreements, managing privileges, and terminating access in a timely manner.
All of these can also minimize risks to USDA information and information systems.
